content.text: {"headline":"Approve P1: a no-cost mix of break shifts, a 2-agent cross-skill loan and IVR callback on General, predicted to lift service level to 82.3% (target 80%) for 12:45-14:45.","why":"The problem is unplanned absence, not demand. Accounts & General has 6 absences against a usual 2.4 per day (2 called in sick, 4 sent home unwell). Agents on the phones dropped to 27 against 33 planned at 12:30, and service level fell to 58.2%. Call volume is roughly normal (+4.7% for the day). If we do nothing, the window is predicted at 79.2%, just under target, with General at 71.6%. P1 delays General breaks in 13:45-14:45 by 45 minutes, moves 2 cross-skilled agents from Payments to General (12:45-15:00) and turns on IVR callback for General. That takes the window to 82.3% and abandons from 5.0% to 4.3% at no extra cost. It is the cheapest plan that meets target and follows policy.","trade_offs":["Cost vs. margin: P1 is free but clears the target by only 2.3 points, and General stays below target at 78.3%. P4 costs INR 630 for 84.5%, with General at 82.2% and 3.9% abandons.","Customer impact: P2 or P3 (INR 3,150 each) give the strongest result: 86.2% and 87.9% overall, General at 83.6% and 87.9%, abandons down to 2.8% and 3.0%.","Other queue: lending 2 agents does not hurt Payments, which is predicted at 85.4% vs 84.8% with no action.","Execution risk: P1 relies on callback uptake and break delays landing as planned; there is no overtime buffer if another agent goes home."],"watch":"Watch General service level and agent headcount through 14:45. If General stays well below 78% or another absence occurs, move to P4 (INR 630) or P2 (INR 3,150) overtime."}
